headline: Exonerated
dek: The President says the Democrats’ attempt to impeach the Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, has failed, with every Republican but Thomas Massie voting for him, and credits victories, record recruitment and “Spirit like rarely seen before”.

original.speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: The Democrats’ attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has miserably FAILED! Every single Republican, except Thomas Massie, a major LOSER, voted in favor of Pete. Again, Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military (Long waiting lists to get in!), and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot. The Democrats continue to weaponize and abuse the United States of America. They must be stopped! MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN. President DONALD J. TRUMP
original.key: The Democrats’ attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has miserably FAILED!
original.context: Posted on the afternoon of 10 November 2026, after the vote on the attempt to impeach the Secretary of War (see “Praised, not impeached” and “A plus, plus, plus”). The figures on recruitment are the President’s.

verification.note: Copied by the editor from truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump on 11 November 2026 (shown as 11/10/26, 3:24 PM Pacific).

en: I welcome the decision not to proceed with the impeachment of Secretary Hegseth, and I thank the members of Congress who supported him.

The Secretary can now return his full attention to our armed forces and to recruitment, which my administration reports is at record levels. I hope that impeachment will be kept for the most serious cases, and that we can now work together.
fr: Je salue la décision de ne pas donner suite à la procédure de destitution du secrétaire Hegseth, et je remercie les membres du Congrès qui l’ont soutenu.

Le secrétaire peut maintenant consacrer toute son attention à nos forces armées et au recrutement, qui atteint, selon mon administration, des niveaux record. J’espère que la destitution sera réservée aux cas les plus graves, et que nous pourrons désormais travailler ensemble.
presidential.key: I welcome the decision not to proceed with the impeachment of Secretary Hegseth, and I thank the members of Congress who supported him.

vaudois.hook: La tentative des démocrates a échoué ! *Bon. Y a pas le feu au lac.*
vaudois.hookEn: The Democrats’ attempt has failed! *Well. No need to rush.*
vaudois.short: Chez nous, quand on gagne, on ne crie pas en majuscules. On dit « ça a joué » et on reprend un verre. *Y a pas le feu au lac.*
vaudois.shortEn: Round here, when you win, you don’t shout in capitals. You say “it went fine” and pour another glass. *No need to rush.*
text: La tentative des démocrates de destituer Pete Hegseth a échoué, et pas qu’un peu. Tous les républicains ont voté pour lui, sauf ce Massie, un grand perdant. Des victoires, un recrutement record, un esprit comme on en voit rarement, à ce que je dis : Pete est blanchi.
Remarquez, chez nous, quand on gagne, on ne crie pas en majuscules. On dit « ça a joué », on reprend un verre de chasselas, et on rentre à la maison. Y a pas le feu au lac.
en: The Democrats’ attempt to impeach Pete Hegseth has failed, and not by a little. Every Republican voted for him, except that Massie, a big loser. Victories, record recruitment, a spirit rarely seen, or so I say: Pete is cleared.
Mind you, round here, when you win, you don’t shout in capital letters. You say “it went fine”, pour another glass of Chasselas and go home. No need to rush.
notes: “Il n’y a pas le feu au lac” (“the lake isn’t on fire”: Lake Geneva) is the classic Vaudois way of saying there is no hurry. “Ça a joué” means “it worked out”.

fribourgeois.hook: Des listes d’attente pour entrer ! *Chez nous, la lettre arrive à 18 ans.*
fribourgeois.hookEn: Waiting lists to get in! *Round here the letter arrives at 18.*
fribourgeois.short: Une liste d’attente pour l’armée ? Chez nous, pas besoin : le service est obligatoire. *La lettre arrive toute seule, que tu veuilles ou non.*
fribourgeois.shortEn: A waiting list for the army? Not here: service is compulsory. *The letter just arrives, like it or not.*
text: Les démocrates voulaient destituer Pete Hegseth : raté, et en beauté ! Tous les républicains ont voté pour lui, sauf ce Massie, un grand perdant. Et le recrutement, le meilleur de l’histoire, je le dis, avec des listes d’attente pour entrer !

Chez nous, une liste d’attente pour l’armée, on ne connaît pas : le service est obligatoire. À 18 ans, la lettre arrive toute seule, que tu veuilles ou non. Le seul endroit où on fait la queue, c’est à la buvette après le tir.
en: The Democrats wanted to impeach Pete Hegseth: a flop, and a grand one! Every Republican voted for him, except that Massie, a big loser. And recruitment is the best in history, I say, with waiting lists to get in!
Round here we don’t know about waiting lists for the army: service is compulsory. At 18, the letter just arrives, like it or not. The only place there’s a queue is at the bar after shooting practice.
notes: Military service is compulsory for Swiss men, who are called up for recruitment at about 18 or 19. Village shooting ranges, with their buvette (bar), are part of Swiss life.

lyonnais.hook: Un esprit comme on en voit rarement ! *Viens à Lyon le 8 décembre.*
lyonnais.hookEn: A spirit rarely seen! *Come to Lyon on the 8th of December.*
lyonnais.short: Un esprit comme on en voit rarement ? Le 8 décembre, toute la ville met des lumignons aux fenêtres. *Et personne ne vote contre.*
lyonnais.shortEn: A spirit rarely seen? On 8 December the whole city puts candles in its windows. *And nobody votes against.*
text: La destitution de Pete Hegseth ? Échec total des démocrates ! Tous les républicains pour lui, sauf ce Massie, un perdant. Des victoires, un recrutement record, et un esprit comme on en voit rarement, je vous le dis.
Un esprit comme on en voit rarement ? Viens à Lyon le 8 décembre, gone : toute la ville met des lumignons aux fenêtres, et on se promène dehors jusqu’à minuit. Et personne ne vote contre.
en: The impeachment of Pete Hegseth? A total failure for the Democrats! Every Republican for him, except that Massie, a loser. Victories, record recruitment and a spirit rarely seen, I tell you.
A spirit rarely seen? Come to Lyon on 8 December, mate: the whole city puts candles in its windows and everyone strolls about until midnight. And nobody votes against.
notes: Every 8 December, the people of Lyon place small candles (lumignons) in their windows: the tradition, since 1852, grew into the Fête des Lumières.

parisien.hook: Blanchi ! *Comme le Sacré-Cœur : il suffit qu’il pleuve.*
parisien.hookEn: Cleared! *Like the Sacré-Cœur: all it takes is rain.*
parisien.short: Blanchi ? À Paris, le Sacré-Cœur se blanchit tout seul : sa pierre devient plus blanche à chaque averse. *Pete, il a fallu un vote.*
parisien.shortEn: Cleared? In Paris the Sacré-Cœur whitens itself: its stone gets whiter with every shower. *Pete needed a vote.*
text: Les démocrates ont voulu destituer Pete Hegseth, et ils se sont plantés, mais alors complètement. Tous les républicains ont voté pour lui, sauf ce Massie. Pete est blanchi, je le dis, et en beauté.
Remarquez, blanchi, à Paris, on connaît : le Sacré-Cœur se blanchit tout seul, sa pierre devient plus blanche à chaque averse. Lui, il lui suffit qu’il pleuve. Pete, il a fallu un vote. Bon, je file.
en: The Democrats tried to impeach Pete Hegseth, and they fell flat, completely. Every Republican voted for him, except that Massie. Pete is cleared, I say, and in style.
Mind you, in Paris we know about being cleared: the Sacré-Cœur whitens itself, its stone getting whiter with every shower. All it needs is rain. Pete needed a vote. Right, I’m off.
notes: The basilica of the Sacré-Cœur, in Montmartre, is built of a limestone that releases calcite in the rain, which keeps it white.

new-york.hook: Long waiting lists to get in! *In New York, that’s a rent-controlled apartment.*
new-york.short: Long waiting lists to get in? In New York, that’s a rent-controlled apartment. *People wait so long they pass the spot on to their kids.*
text: They tried to impeach Pete Hegseth and it failed, big. Every Republican voted for him except Massie, a major loser. Best recruitment in history, I’m telling you. Long waiting lists to get in!
Waiting lists? Please. In New York, a waiting list is a rent-controlled apartment. People wait so long they leave the spot to their kids. You want a waiting list, I’ll give you a waiting list.
en: He celebrates the failed impeachment, attacks the one Republican who voted against, and repeats his claims of record recruitment with waiting lists.
To a New Yorker, a real waiting list is the one for a rent-regulated apartment, which can last for years.

deep-south.hook: Spirit like rarely seen before! *Honey, you’ve never been to an SEC game.*
deep-south.short: Spirit like rarely seen? Honey, come down on a Saturday in the fall. *A hundred thousand people singing the fight song in the heat.*
text: Well, that impeachment business went nowhere, bless their hearts. Every Republican stood by Pete, except that Massie, poor thing. And the spirit, why, I’ve rarely seen anything like it.
Spirit like rarely seen before? Honey, come down on a Saturday in the fall, when a hundred thousand folks are singing the fight song in the heat. Now that’s spirit. Bring a folding chair.
en: With exaggerated Southern politeness, he dismisses the failed impeachment and its one Republican supporter, and praises a “spirit rarely seen”.
In the South, the real spirit is college football: on autumn Saturdays, the big Southeastern Conference stadiums hold around a hundred thousand fans.

wales.hook: Long waiting lists to get in! *Try getting a ticket for Wales against England.*
wales.short: Long waiting lists to get in? Try getting a ticket for Wales against England in Cardiff. *Now that’s a waiting list.*
text: The impeachment of Pete Hegseth has failed, it has. Every Republican voted for him, except that Massie, a proper loser. Best recruitment ever, I’m telling you, with long waiting lists to get in.

Long waiting lists, is it? Try getting a ticket for Wales against England at the stadium in Cardiff. Now that’s a waiting list. And the spirit? You’ve heard nothing until you’ve heard the anthem there.
en: He celebrates the failed impeachment, mocks the lone Republican dissenter, and boasts of waiting lists to join the military.
To the Welsh, the hardest ticket to get is a Wales–England rugby match in Cardiff, where the national anthem is famously sung by the whole stadium.

british-diplomat.hook: EXONERATION! *In Westminster, ministers are more usually reshuffled.*
british-diplomat.short: Ministers in Westminster are seldom exonerated. *They are more usually reshuffled, which is quieter, and nobody needs capital letters.*
british-diplomat.shortEn: He won the vote. *In capital letters.*
text: His Majesty’s Government notes that the attempt to impeach the Secretary of War has concluded.
We would observe that ministers in Westminster are seldom exonerated. They are more usually reshuffled, which is quieter, and requires no capital letters.
en: He would like everyone to know it, in capital letters.

text: France takes note of the outcome of the procedure in the United States Congress.

We would simply observe that when an institution examines the conduct of a minister and reaches a conclusion, it is democracy that has worked, whatever the result. In France, ministers may answer for acts in office before a special court; we have learned that it is a sign of health, not of weakness.
fr: La France prend acte de l’issue de la procédure au Congrès des États-Unis.

Nous observerons simplement que lorsqu’une institution examine la conduite d’un ministre et parvient à une conclusion, c’est la démocratie qui a fonctionné, quel que soit le résultat. En France, les ministres peuvent répondre des actes de leur fonction devant une cour spéciale ; nous avons appris que c’est un signe de santé, non de faiblesse.
notes: In France, the Cour de justice de la République tries members of the government for offences committed in the exercise of their duties.

text: The Federal Council takes note of the vote.

Switzerland has no Secretary of War, and no general either: Parliament elects one only in time of war. It has done so four times since 1848. In between, the army is run by a civilian department, which also looks after sport.
fr: Le Conseil fédéral prend acte du vote.

La Suisse n’a pas de secrétaire à la Guerre, ni même de général : le Parlement n’en élit un qu’en temps de guerre. Il l’a fait quatre fois depuis 1848. Entre-temps, l’armée dépend d’un département civil, qui s’occupe aussi du sport.
notes: Switzerland’s Federal Assembly elects a general only in time of war or of serious threat: Dufour, Herzog, Wille and Guisan.
